conflicts: The durations given for the missing time are mutually inconsistent within a single episode: nine hours in the video description, five hours in the narration at 00:01:02 and five and a half at 00:55:39. The elapsed-year figures likewise: fifty in the title, forty-nine in the narration at 00:04:08, forty-eight and a half from Woods at 00:08:07. No figure is adopted here.

The production's narration describes the object as a massive glowing red orb; Woods's and Johnson's waking descriptions do not match that, and the narration is the publisher's voice rather than a witness's.

label: Mario Woods
narrative: Mario Woods is the long-standing claimant of the Ellsworth case and he is the clean example of what CLAUDE.md section 2a was widened to admit: a named man with a thirty-year dated public record of the same account, and no service record produced. He says that on 18 November 1977 at about 0100 he and a fellow security policeman of the 44th Missile Security Squadron responded to an alarm at Launch Facility November-5 in the Ellsworth Minuteman field, that a large bright object hovered under about fifty feet over the site, that humanoid figures approached the truck, that both men were taken aboard and examined, that hours were lost, and that both were recovered about eight miles away beside a reservoir dam and interrogated separately on base. NO AIR FORCE RECORD OF THE EVENT HAS EVER BEEN PRODUCED BY ANYONE, and no service record for Woods has been opened by this board. What is dated is the telling: he has given the account publicly since 1996 and claims more than forty media appearances, he named his partner Michael Johnson on air for years and asked audiences to find him, the board already carries his 5 July 2025 American Alchemy appearance including his statement that an OSI man named Rick Doty was at his debrief, and he appears again on Jesse Michels's episode of 7 September 2026. That is the anchor: the dated artefact of the claim, not a record of the thing claimed.
